title: Electrochemical Cell Voltage Comparison Lab
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that simulates an electrochemical cell voltage comparison laboratory where users can swap electrode materials, control elapsed time, and observe voltage/current behavior with strict electrochemical accuracy.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 10) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Render on a dark navy background (#0a0a2a).
- Create a lab bench (flat box, wood-brown color) centered at y=0.

ELECTROCHEMICAL CELLS:
- Display TWO electrochemical cells side by side on the bench, Cell A at x=-3 and Cell B at x=3.
- Each cell consists of:
  - A transparent beaker (cylinder with transparent blue-tinted material, opacity 0.3).
  - Two electrode rods inserted into the beaker (thin cylinders, colored by material).
  - A wire connecting the two electrodes (curved line above the beaker).
  - A small voltmeter box between the electrodes on the wire (box with a display face).
  - Animated bubble particles rising inside the beaker (small spheres moving upward, rate proportional to current).
  - Electrolyte solution shown as a semi-transparent volume inside the beaker.

ELECTRODE MATERIALS (each cell independently selectable):
- Zinc (Zn): gray color, standard reduction potential = -0.76V
- Copper (Cu): orange-brown color, standard reduction potential = +0.34V
- Silver (Ag): silver/white color, standard reduction potential = +0.80V
- Iron (Fe): dark gray color, standard reduction potential = -0.44V
- Lead (Pb): blue-gray color, standard reduction potential = -0.13V
- Platinum (Pt): platinum/light-gray color, standard reduction potential = +1.20V

VOLTAGE CALCULATION:
- Cell EMF = E_cathode - E_anode, where cathode is the electrode with higher reduction potential and anode is the lower.
- The left electrode in each cell is the anode, the right is the cathode. If the user picks materials such that the left has higher potential, the cell voltage is negative (reversed polarity), and the voltmeter should show a negative value.
- Actual formula: cellVoltage = rightElectrodeReductionPotential - leftElectrodeReductionPotential.

TIME CONTROL:
- A simulation clock starting at t=0 seconds.
- A slider (range input) at the bottom of the screen labeled 'Time (s)' from 0 to 600 seconds.
- A Play/Pause button that auto-advances time at 1 simulated second per real 100ms.
- A Reset button that sets time back to 0.
- Over time, voltage degrades slightly: effectiveVoltage = cellVoltage * (1 - 0.0003 * time). This models concentration polarization.
- Current (amps) = effectiveVoltage / 2.0 (internal resistance = 2 ohms). Can be negative if voltage is negative.
- Bubble rate in each cell = Math.abs(current) * 10 bubbles visible at any time (clamped 0-30).

INTERACTIONS:
- DOM dropdown selects for each cell's left and right electrode material (4 dropdowns total): #cellA-left, #cellA-right, #cellB-left, #cellB-right.
- Clicking on a cell's beaker in the 3D scene highlights that cell (yellow outline or emissive glow) and shows its details in a HUD panel.
- Keyboard 'A' selects Cell A, 'B' selects Cell B.
- Keyboard 'R' resets time to 0.
- Keyboard Space toggles play/pause.
- A 'Swap Electrodes' button (#swap-btn) that swaps the left and right electrode materials of the currently selected cell.
- An 'Undo' button (#undo-btn) that reverts the last electrode material change (maintain a history stack of up to 20 changes).
- A 'Redo' button (#redo-btn) that re-applies the last undone change.

HUD / UI PANEL:
- Top-right panel showing for the selected cell:
  - Cell name (A or B)
  - Left electrode material and its reduction potential
  - Right electrode material and its reduction potential
  - Calculated EMF (cellVoltage)
  - Effective voltage at current time
  - Current (amps)
  - Polarity indicator: 'Normal' if cellVoltage >= 0, 'Reversed' if < 0
- Bottom bar with the time slider, play/pause, reset, swap, undo, redo buttons.
- A comparison panel (#comparison-panel) showing: 'Cell A EMF: X.XXV | Cell B EMF: X.XXV | Difference: X.XXV'

STATE MANAGEMENT (window.__3D_STATE__):
Expose the following on every frame update:
{
  sceneReady: true,
  time: <number>,  // current simulation time in seconds
  isPlaying: <boolean>,
  selectedCell: 'A' | 'B',
  cellA: {
    leftMaterial: <string>,   // e.g. 'Zn'
    rightMaterial: <string>,  // e.g. 'Cu'
    leftPotential: <number>,  // e.g. -0.76
    rightPotential: <number>, // e.g. 0.34
    cellVoltage: <number>,    // right - left potential
    effectiveVoltage: <number>, // with time degradation
    current: <number>,        // effectiveVoltage / 2.0
    polarity: 'Normal' | 'Reversed',
    bubbleCount: <number>     // active bubbles
  },
  cellB: { /* same structure */ },
  voltageDifference: <number>, // Math.abs(cellA.cellVoltage - cellB.cellVoltage)
  historyStackSize: <number>,  // undo stack length
  redoStackSize: <number>,     // redo stack length
  totalObjects: <number>,      // total meshes in scene
  energyConservation: <boolean> // true if |effectiveVoltage| <= |cellVoltage| for both cells
}

Default initial state: Cell A = Zn(left)/Cu(right), Cell B = Fe(left)/Ag(right), time=0, selectedCell='A', isPlaying=false.

ENSURE:
- All voltages are computed to at least 4 decimal places internally.
- No NaN or Infinity values ever appear in state.
- Bubble animations are smooth and proportional to current magnitude.
- Electrode colors update immediately when materials change.
- The comparison panel updates in real-time.
- Conservation: effectiveVoltage magnitude never exceeds cellVoltage magnitude.
- History stack properly tracks material changes for undo/redo.
physics_constraints: Cell EMF = E_right - E_left using standard reduction potentials. Effective voltage degrades as V_eff = V_cell * (1 - 0.0003*t). Current = V_eff / 2.0 (R_internal=2Ω). Bubble count = clamp(|current|*10, 0, 30). Energy conservation: |V_eff| <= |V_cell| at all times. No NaN/Infinity in any computed value. Polarity reversal when left electrode has higher reduction potential than right.
